## Animals are *animate*

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Animal actions influence 
  - The external world, $W$
  - Their own bodies, $B$
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  N[Nervous System] --> B[Body]
  B --> W[World]
```
:::
::::

---

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Nervous system *outputs*
  - Autonomic
  - Endocrine
  - Somatic
:::
::: {.column width=50%}

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  N[Nervous System] -- autonomic --> B[Body];
  N -- somatic --> B;
  N -- endocrine --> B;
```

:::
::::

---

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Nervous system *inputs* fall into two broad classes.

:::
::: {.column width=50%}
```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  N[Nervous System] <---|interoception| B[Body]
  N <---|exteroception| B
```
:::
::::

---

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  N[Nervous System] -- autonomic --> B[Body]
  N -- somatic --> B
  N -- endocrine --> B
  B --->|interoception| N
  B --->|action| W[World]
  W --->|perception| B
  B --->|exteroception| N
```

## What actions must animals perform?

- Live long enough to reproduce

---

::: {.incremental}
- Living long enough...
  - Avoid injury & predation
  - Secure sustenance
  - Maintain health
- Reproducing...
  - Find a mate
  - Mate
  - Ensure the well-being of offspring
- In other words, *behaving*
:::

# Illustrative motor systems

## Looking

- Behavioral goals
  - Direct gaze (eyes + head + body) toward goal-relevant targets
  - Direct gaze toward emergent targets
  - Track/pursue targets across observer/target motion
  - Maximize quality of visual information about targets

---

## Eye movements

::: {.incremental}
- Voluntary
  - Saccades
  - Smooth pursuit
  - Vergence
- Involuntary
  - Vestibulo-occular reflex (VOR)
  - Optokinetic nystagmus
  - Accommodation
:::

## Saccades

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Rapid, ballistic (no online feedback)
- ~2-3/s
- ~200 ms to initiate
- Amplitudes >20 deg $\rightarrow$ saccade + head movement
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
{{< video https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e9/This_shows_a_recording_of_the_eye_movements_of_a_participant_looking_freely_at_a_picture.webm >}}
:::
::::

-- @Wikipedia-contributors2025-mr

## Vergence

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Eyes move disjointly
- Fixate on comparable locations
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![CC BY-SA 3.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=74230](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0e/Stereogram_Tut_Eye_Convergence.png){width=70%}
:::
::::

## Vestibulo-occular reflex (VOR)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Steady eyes when head moves
- Fast: response < 10 ms
- Disturbed in vertigo
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![By .Koen - Own work based on: Simple vestibulo-ocular reflex.PNG and Image:ThreeNeuronArc.png, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=4130081](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Vestibulo-ocular_reflex_EN.svg/1280px-Vestibulo-ocular_reflex_EN.svg.png){width=50% fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

## Pupil constriction/dilation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Bright light $\rightarrow$ constriction
  - Also by parasympathetic activation
- Dim light $\rightarrow$ dilation
  - Also by sympathetic activation
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![By Greyson Orlando - Own work, Public Domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=1451923](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a3/Eye_dilate.gif)
:::
::::

## Eye muscles

![](https://pressbooks.library.torontomu.ca/assessmentnursingmain/wp-content/uploads/sites/421/2024/08/Extraocular-movement-via-cranial-nerves.jpg){width=90%}

---

|  Nerve |  Eye Muscle|
|------------|---------------|
|  CN III Oculomotor | Superior rectus |
|   | Inferior rectus |
|  | Medial rectus |
|  | Inferior oblique |
|  | Iris (pupillary) sphincter |
| CN IV Trochlear | Superior oblique | 
| CN VI Abducens | Lateral rectus | 
| ANS sympathetic | Iris (pupillary) dilator |

## Inputs to CN III

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["Frontal Eye Fields"] -->|"Voluntary saccades"| B(("CN III"))
  C["Superior Colliculus"] -->|"Reflexive saccades"| B
  D["Vestibular (CN VIII) n."] -->|"VOR"|B
  B --> E["Superior rectus"]
  B --> F["Inferior rectus"]
  B --> G["Medial rectus"]
  B --> H["Inferior oblique"]
  I["Parasympathetic NS"] -.-> B
  B -.-> J["Iris (pupillary) sphincter"]
```

## Considerations

- Act to perceive; perceive to act
- Provide sensory feedback
  - Move eyes $\rightarrow$ shift visual field
  - Change vergence or lens thickness $\rightarrow$ change image focus
  - Eye muscles (probably) have proprioceptors analogous to spindles in skeletal muscles

## Considerations

- Relatively simple physics: 
  - Limited influence of gravity, friction
- Small # of muscles $\rightarrow$ "model" motor system?
- **DEMO**: Illustrates "forward" model?
  - Predicting future sensory states
